fullPassage: The idea that our senses may be deceiving us was taken up by the French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes. (C) He realized that sometimes our senses give us a false impression — a straight stick in a glass of water appears to be bent, for example. And if we know that they can be unreliable, it would be wrong to trust them completely — everything that we experience with our senses might be false. (A) It might even be that we are asleep, and that the world we are experiencing is no more than a dream, or that God or some mischievous power is making us believe things that are not really true. If that is the case, though, we can never know anything for sure. (B) But Descartes then showed that there was one thing he could be sure of: In order to be deceived, he must exist, and exist as a thing that thinks. So, although his senses could not be trusted, he could be sure he existed as something that was capable of thinking and reasoning.

He realized that sometimes our senses give us a false impression. And if we know that they can be __________ (rely), it would be wrong to trust them completely — everything that we experience with our senses might be false.

det.korean: rely(의지하다) → unreliable(믿을 수 없는). 문맥상 감각을 신뢰할 수 없다는 뜻.
det.analysis: can be + 형용사(보어). rely → reliable → unreliable (부정 접두사 un-). 문맥상 '믿을 수 없는'.
det.tip: rely → reliable(믿을 수 있는) → unreliable(믿을 수 없는)

questions.passage: The idea that our senses may be __________ us was taken up by the French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes. He realized that sometimes our senses give us a false impression — a straight stick in a glass of water appears to be bent, for example. And if we know that they can be unreliable, it would be wrong to trust them completely — everything that we experience with our senses might be false. It might even be that we are asleep, and that the world we are experiencing is no more than a dream, or that God or some mischievous power is making us believe things that are not really true. If that is the case, though, we can never know anything for sure. But Descartes then showed that there was one thing he could be sure of: In order to be deceived, he must exist, and exist as a thing that thinks. So, although his senses could not be trusted, he could be sure he existed as something that was capable of thinking and reasoning.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: deceiving(속이다): 우리의 감각이 우리를 속이고 있을 수도 있다는 생각
det.analysis:
✅ ① deceiving: 원문 그대로 (may be deceiving us)
❌ ② guiding: 안내하다 — 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ helping: 돕다 — 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ informing: 알리다 — 문맥 부적절
det.tip: deceive = mislead / trick (속이다)

det.korean: 사고와 추론이 가능한 존재로 자신이 존재한다는 것을 확신할 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② he existed as something capable of thinking and reasoning
❌ ① his senses were always accurate and reliable
❌ ③ the world around him was definitely real
❌ ④ dreams and reality were impossible to distinguish
✅① he existed as something capable of thinking: 원문과 일치
❌② senses accurate: 감각은 신뢰 불가
❌③ world was real: 확실하지 않음
❌④ impossible to distinguish: 구별 불가가 결론이 아님
det.tip: 데카르트의 결론: 감각은 못 믿지만 '생각하는 존재'로서의 자신은 확실히 존재.
